entries.note: E38 (spec-entity-fields-12plus.md), first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. plantShield is a long magnitude like arm1/arm2 (extra hit points ahead of the entity's real health pool), so it is priced on the same reference scale those already use: one shield point costs the same as one armor point until a sweep says otherwise.

E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. LowerIsBetter timer (structural floor, same reason attackInterval has one); referenceScale 1 mirrors stat.derived's own 'one resolver point' scale rather than arm1's, because a countdown in seconds is a much smaller natural range than a hit-point pool.

E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. A signed delta with no floor (unguarded by design, spec §2b) -- small numbers matter here, so referenceScale 1 keeps a modest adder from pricing as noise.
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Same reasoning as attackCountdown: LowerIsBetter timer, structural floor, small natural range.

E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Most plants never move, so a baseline of zero is ordinary (see StatComposer's own Real() note) -- when it does apply, movement speed is a small natural range, referenceScale 1.
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Same reasoning as plantSpeed.
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. A long magnitude, priced on arm1/maxHp's own reference scale -- a level-up is a meaningful, discrete magnitude change, not a fractional ratio.
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Same reasoning as plantLevel.

E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Conceptually the same family as the existing 'defense' channel (a flat mitigation stat), so it is priced on defense's own reference scale rather than arm1's hit-point scale.

E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Bearer frame (decided 2026-09-03, spec-entity-fields-12plus.md sec 2c): this channel stays LowerIsBetter, so a RAISE on your OWN takeDmgMultiplier prices as a penalty and a REDUCTION prices as a benefit -- both correct under the bearer frame. takeDmgMultiplier is NOT the authoring surface for 'enemies take more damage': that debuff is a status.apply payload, priced by its own coefficient/trigger/uptime, never a stat.modify on this channel. Reference scale mirrors 'defense' (same damage-mitigation family).
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Mirrors the existing zombieSpeed (uniqueSpeed) channel's own small natural range.
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Same reasoning as zombieSpeedCurrent.

E41 (spec-ui-attach-point.md sec 2c), authored -- not a fitted sweep result, and never will be. A present is read-only: it never writes stat/resource/status/shield/board/currency state, so it is worth exactly zero power, deliberately, in both directions -- a UI atom must not become a free rider that inflates a container's apparent budget, and it must not tax one either. This row exists so CoefficientTable.Find returns an AUTHORED zero (verdict Priced) rather than falling through to the channel-less-row-missing case (verdict unpriced) -- an authored zero and a missing row are different claims, and this row is what keeps them different. Do not delete this row to 'simplify' -- ui.present has PowerCategory.None (AtomKindRegistryTests.cs's own cosmetic exemption), and a missing coefficient here is the exact PLANTED_VIOLATION this module's own pricing test guards against.
